title: Studio Museum in Harlem Capital Campaign
desc: The Studio Museum is raising $300M+ for a new building designed by Adjaye Associates, an expanded endowment, and operating reserves.

title: DonorsChoose Classroom Project Funding for Public School Teachers
desc: Leading crowdfunding platform where public school teachers create project requests for classroom supplies, technology, and field trips.

title: Harlem Children's Zone Promise Academy Expansion
desc: Comprehensive cradle-to-career pipeline including Promise Academy charter schools (K-12). Challenge grant matches donations up to $10K.

title: RFP: Global Health and Wellbeing in an Era of Transformative AI
desc: $10-30M RFP for research, policy, and field-building to ensure AI improves human health globally. Deadline: August 21, 2026.

title: Khan Academy Learners Fund — Expanding AI-Powered Tutoring
desc: Funding to scale Khanmigo AI tutoring to millions more students. Seeking corporate and foundation partnerships.

title: 2026 Housing Affordability Breakthrough Challenge
desc: $10M across five organizations ($2M each) for scalable housing innovations.

title: 2026 People-First AI Fund
desc: $50M fund for U.S. nonprofits using AI for education, health, economic opportunity. Grants $100K-$500K.

title: FY 2026 Children's Mental Health Initiative (CMHI)
desc: SAMHSA announced $69.1M including $43M for CMHI, Zero Suicide, and Assisted Outpatient Treatment.

title: MEAF National Grant Program: Careers in Technology for Youth with Disabilities
desc: Funds nonprofits developing youth leadership and employment skills, helping young people with disabilities (and veterans with disabilities) transition into competitive technology careers. Grants of $10K-$100K/year for 1-2 years; proposals due Nov. 1 for projects starting the following April.

title: BJA FY 2026 Kevin and Avonte Program
org: Bureau of Justice Assistance (U.S. Dept. of Justice)
desc: Federal grants of up to $150K over 36 months to reduce injury and death among missing individuals with dementia and developmental disabilities (e.g. tracking technology, first-responder training, caregiver resources).

title: Transformation of Mental Health Care Program
desc: Funds academic researchers and institutions piloting innovative models of child and adolescent mental health care (including ADHD and depression). Up to $100K/year for 2 years ($200K total); application portal opens Aug. 15 each year.

title: Direct Action Visionary Grants
desc: Funds community-based interventions grounded in psychological science, including trauma-informed care and mental health support for underserved and immigrant communities. Grants up to $60,000.

title: SFARI New Ideas Award
location: United States (faculty at accredited institutions; excludes China/Hong Kong)
desc: Supports early-stage, exploratory research testing novel hypotheses in autism and related neurodevelopmental disorders. Up to $300K/year for 2 years ($600K total). Letters of intent accepted on a rolling basis; researchers new to autism research are especially encouraged to apply.

title: Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation Grants: Nutrition Education, Food Access & Culinary Careers
desc: Funds 501(c)(3) nonprofits whose primary mission is nutrition education, improving access to food, or advancing careers in the culinary arts. Applications due November 1, 2026 for awards in 2027.

title: Food Access Infrastructure Initiative Grant
location: Northeast U.S. (CT, ME, MA, NH, NJ, NY, RI, VT)
desc: Grants of up to $50,000 to food banks, food hubs, and other nonprofit food distribution organizations for capital infrastructure such as cooler storage and produce handling. Excludes vehicles, food production or processing equipment, and operating costs.

title: Museums for America (FY2027)
org: Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS)
desc: Federal grants of $5,000-$350,000 for museums to strengthen collections, exhibitions, education programs, and community engagement over one to three years. Requires 1:1 non-federal cost share.

title: Humanity AI Open Call: Communities Leading on AI
org: Humanity AI (Ford, MacArthur, Mellon, Mozilla and other funders)
desc: $10M open call for U.S. 501(c)(3) lead applicants running community-led projects that shape how AI is built, governed, and used in education, labor, and arts and culture. Grants of $75,000-$1,000,000 for up to three years.

title: Atlassian Foundation Open Call: Collective Action for Education in the AI Era
desc: Open call for registered nonprofits working in collective action initiatives to help disadvantaged learners thrive in the AI era. Up to US$1M over two years per partnership, plus a peer learning cohort.
